Careers At Bigwigs Build Your Career. Build The Future. Together. Join a team of passionate engineers, AI experts, designers, and innovators building intelligent products that empower businesses globally. Apply Now Bigwigs Technologies

How does the hiring process work? Our process starts with an application review, followed by a technical assessment, one or more interviews with the team, and a final offer. We aim to keep every stage transparent and give you feedback along the way.

What technologies do you use? Our stack spans modern frontend frameworks, cloud-native backend services, and AI/ML tooling for data annotation, computer vision, and Generative AI — the exact tools vary by team and role.

Can freshers apply? Yes. Several of our roles, especially in Data Operations and Engineering, are open to freshers with strong fundamentals and a willingness to learn. We look for potential as much as experience.
Do you offer remote work? Many of our roles support remote or hybrid work. Each job listing specifies its location and work arrangement so you know what to expect before applying.
How long does recruitment take? Most candidates move through our process within two to three weeks, though timelines can vary depending on the role and interview scheduling.

Healthcare Scaling AI Data Annotation for a Computer Vision Project A HIPAA-compliant medical image annotation pipeline that trained a radiology triage model to flag critical findings in under two minutes. Medical Image Annotation DICOM Processing Global AI Technology Company The client needed a large volume of accurately annotated image datasets to train a computer vision model. Internal resources were insufficient to meet aggressive delivery timelines. Aggressive delivery timeline outpaced internal annotation capacity Radiology-grade accuracy required on every labeled study PHI-sensitive DICOM data demanded strict de-identification No existing multi-tier QA process for clinical-grade validation Bigwigs stood up a dedicated medical annotation pod combining radiology-trained annotators, a multi-tier QA review process, and an automated DICOM de-identification pipeline — giving the client a continuously validated, clinically defensible training dataset. Data Ingestion & De-identification Secure intake of DICOM studies with automated PHI stripping and audit logging. Annotation Protocol Design Clinical taxonomy and labeling guidelines co-developed with the client's lead radiologists. Multi-Tier Radiologist QA Every study passes through primary annotation, peer review, and a final radiologist sign-off. Model Training Handoff Structured export pipelines feeding directly into the client's training environment. Continuous Feedback Loop Model error analysis routed back into annotator retraining each sprint. DICOM De-identification Multi-Tier QA Review Model Validation Support CVAT OHIF Viewer pydicom Python Radiology-trained annotators QA leads Project manager ML liaison Annotation Accuracy 99.4% Inter-Annotator Agreement 97.2% QA Pass Rate 98.8% Avg. Turnaround Triage Speed 3.5x faster Critical findings flagged in under two minutes. Model Accuracy Gain +14% Improvement in diagnostic model precision. Radiologist Hours Saved 1,200+/mo Freed up for high-complexity cases.

Automotive LiDAR & Sensor Fusion Annotation for Autonomous Driving A high-throughput 3D point cloud and camera-LiDAR fusion annotation pipeline built for a Tier-1 autonomous vehicle supplier. LiDAR Annotation Sensor Fusion Tier-1 Autonomous Vehicle Supplier A Tier-1 autonomous vehicle supplier needed millions of frames of synchronized camera and LiDAR data annotated to train perception models for highway and urban driving scenarios. Existing annotation throughput couldn't keep pace with the volume of sensor data generated by the test fleet, and cross-sensor labeling consistency between camera bounding boxes and 3D point cloud cuboids was inconsistent across vendors. Annotation throughput couldn't match test-fleet data volume Inconsistent camera-to-LiDAR label alignment across vendors No process for surfacing safety-critical edge cases Manual review couldn't scale to millions of frames Bigwigs built a dedicated 3D annotation team trained on multi-sensor calibration, introduced a fusion-aware QA layer that cross-validates camera and LiDAR labels against each other, and mined edge cases to prioritize the highest-value frames first. Multi-Sensor Calibration Review Verifying camera-LiDAR extrinsics before any frame enters the queue. 3D Point Cloud Labeling Cuboid annotation of vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, and static obstacles. Camera-LiDAR Fusion QA Cross-sensor consistency checks between 2D boxes and 3D cuboids. Edge Case Mining Active-learning driven surfacing of rare and safety-critical scenarios. Model Feedback Integration Perception model failure cases routed back into annotation priorities. 3D LiDAR Annotation Camera-LiDAR Fusion Edge Case Curation Scenario Tagging SuperAnnotate Custom Fusion Pipeline Python ROS Bag Tooling 3D annotation specialists Sensor fusion QA Data scientist Delivery lead Point Cloud Accuracy 99.1% Cross-Sensor Consistency 96.5% QA Pass Rate 98.2% Frames Processed / Day Annotation Throughput 4.2x Increase after workflow re-engineering. Model mAP Improvement +11.3% On pedestrian and cyclist detection. Cost per Frame -38% Reduction via automation-assisted labeling.

Retail Visual Product Recognition & Catalog Automation An automated pre-labeling and human-in-the-loop QA pipeline that cut catalog processing time by 65% for a global marketplace. Computer Vision Image Classification Global E-Commerce Marketplace A global e-commerce marketplace needed millions of seller-submitted product images classified, tagged, and mapped into a unified taxonomy to power visual search and recommendations. Inconsistent seller-submitted imagery and a fragmented internal taxonomy meant products were frequently mis-categorized, hurting search relevance and slowing time-to-list for new inventory. Inconsistent seller-submitted product imagery Fragmented taxonomy causing frequent mis-categorization Search relevance suffering from inaccurate tagging Slow time-to-list for new inventory Bigwigs redesigned the taxonomy in partnership with the client's catalog team, deployed a custom pre-labeling model to auto-tag high-confidence attributes, and layered human review only where model confidence dropped below threshold. Catalog Audit & Taxonomy Mapping Rebuilding the product taxonomy against real seller inventory. Bounding Box & Attribute Labeling Tagging product region, category, color, and material attributes. Automated Pre-Labeling Pipeline Model-assisted first-pass labeling to reduce manual load. Human-in-the-Loop QA Review focused on low-confidence and ambiguous predictions. Deployment Support Validation of tagged data against live search relevance metrics. Product Image Annotation Attribute Tagging Taxonomy Design Automated Pre-Labeling Label Studio CVAT Python Custom Pre-Labeling Models Category specialists QA analysts ML engineer Project manager Labeling Accuracy 98.9% Attribute Consistency 97.6% QA Pass Rate 99.0% Items Labeled / Day Catalog Processing Time -65% Reduction in time-to-list for new inventory. Search Relevance +22% Improvement in visual search accuracy. Manual Review Load -70% After pre-labeling automation went live.

Finance Document Intelligence & Fraud Detection NLP An entity-annotation and OCR-correction pipeline powering a digital bank's fraud detection and compliance review models. Document AI Regional Digital Banking Platform A regional digital banking platform needed a labeled corpus of financial documents and transaction narratives to train NLP models for fraud pattern detection and automated compliance review. Scanned statements and correspondence had inconsistent OCR quality, and the client's compliance team couldn't manually label the volume of documents needed to reach production-grade model accuracy. Inconsistent OCR quality across scanned statements Compliance team couldn't scale manual labeling Insufficient labeled examples of known fraud typologies Production-grade accuracy required before model deployment Bigwigs combined an OCR correction pass with entity and intent annotation performed by reviewers trained on the client's compliance definitions, then layered fraud-pattern tagging to give the model labeled examples of known fraud typologies. Document Corpus Collection Aggregating statements, applications, and correspondence for labeling. Entity & Intent Annotation Tagging named entities, transaction intents, and risk indicators. OCR Correction Pipeline Human-verified correction of low-confidence OCR extractions. Fraud Pattern Labeling Tagging documents against known fraud typologies for supervised training. Model Validation Support Joint error analysis sessions with the client's data science team. Named Entity Annotation OCR Correction Fraud Pattern Tagging Intent Classification Label Studio Tesseract OCR spaCy Python NLP annotators Compliance-domain reviewers QA lead ML liaison Entity Extraction Accuracy 98.3% OCR Correction Rate 99.5% QA Pass Rate 98.6% Documents Processed / Day Fraud Detection Recall +27% Increase in flagged fraudulent transactions. Manual Review Time -54% Reduction in compliance team workload. False Positives -31% Drop in flagged legitimate transactions.

Agriculture Satellite & Drone Crop Health Monitoring A geospatial segmentation pipeline fusing satellite and drone imagery to power early crop stress detection at scale. GIS & Geospatial Drone Imagery Precision Agriculture Technology Provider A precision agriculture technology provider needed field boundaries, crop types, and stress regions labeled across a multi-source imagery pipeline spanning satellite passes and drone flyovers. Aligning satellite and drone imagery at different resolutions and revisit rates made consistent field-level labeling difficult, and the client's agronomists couldn't scale manual review across every growing region. Satellite and drone imagery at mismatched resolutions Inconsistent revisit rates across imagery sources Agronomists couldn't scale review across every region Field-level labeling consistency was difficult to maintain Bigwigs built a geospatial annotation workflow combining GIS-trained analysts with agronomy-informed reviewers, standardizing field boundary and crop-stress labels across both imagery sources with rigorous geospatial alignment QA. Multi-Source Imagery Ingestion Aligning satellite passes and drone flyovers into a shared pipeline. Field Boundary & Crop Segmentation Semantic segmentation of parcels and crop types. Disease & Stress Region Labeling Tagging stress, disease, and irrigation anomalies with agronomist input. Geospatial QA & Validation Cross-checking annotations against ground-truth coordinates. Model Handoff & Field Testing Supporting validation against live field-scouting reports. Semantic Segmentation Geospatial Annotation Crop Health Tagging Field Boundary Mapping QGIS CVAT Python GDAL GIS analysts Agronomy-informed annotators QA lead Project manager Segmentation Accuracy (IoU) 94.8% Geospatial Alignment 99.2% QA Pass Rate 97.9% Hectares Processed / Week Yield Prediction Accuracy +19% Improvement in early-season forecasts. Field Scouting Time -58% Reduction via automated stress detection. Water Usage Efficiency +15% From targeted irrigation insights.

Smart Cities Traffic & Public Safety Computer Vision A city-scale video annotation and object-tracking pipeline supporting real-time traffic and incident intelligence. Computer Vision Video Annotation Object Tracking Real-Time Analytics Metropolitan Transportation Authority A metropolitan transportation authority needed thousands of hours of multi-camera intersection footage annotated to train object-tracking and incident-detection models for its traffic management center. Footage volume from hundreds of intersections far outpaced the authority's internal review capacity, and existing labels lacked the temporal consistency required for reliable multi-frame object tracking. Footage volume from hundreds of intersections outpaced review capacity Existing labels lacked temporal consistency for tracking No unified taxonomy for incident-event tagging Manual review couldn't keep up with live camera feeds Bigwigs deployed a video annotation team specialized in multi-object tracking, introduced incident-event tagging aligned to the authority's response taxonomy, and validated tracking consistency across full video sequences rather than single frames. Multi-Camera Footage Ingestion Aggregating and indexing footage from intersection camera feeds. Object Detection & Tracking Annotation Frame-consistent labeling of vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists. Incident Event Tagging Tagging collisions, near-misses, and congestion events. Edge Deployment QA Validating annotations against edge-model inference behavior. Live Monitoring Support Ongoing review cycles as new camera feeds came online. Video Frame Annotation Incident Tagging Edge Model Validation CVAT SuperAnnotate Python Custom Tracking Pipeline Video annotators Tracking QA analysts ML liaison Delivery lead Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) 93.6% Detection Precision 98.1% QA Pass Rate 98.4% Hours Annotated / Week 1,100 Incident Response Time -41% Faster detection-to-dispatch. Traffic Flow Optimization +17% Improvement at monitored intersections. False Alarm Rate -35% Reduction in system-generated alerts.
